# Firefox import fixtures

| File | SHA-256 |
| --- | --- |
| `logins.csv` | `c9e59b7b5a0bcea8393000cecce96bfa00a62a6d0604b7334520427b0baac85d` |

## Provenance

**This is not a capture of a live export.** It is generated byte-for-byte from
Mozilla's exporter, by reimplementing `LoginExport._buildCSVRow` and
`LoginExport.exportAsCSV` and feeding it fabricated logins. Read that as the
provenance it is: the *format* is authoritative, the *data* is invented.

| Field | Value |
| --- | --- |
| Schema source | `toolkit/components/passwordmgr/LoginExport.sys.mjs` (mozilla-central / gecko-dev, `master`) |
| Byte-level corroboration | `toolkit/components/passwordmgr/test/unit/test_module_LoginExport.js`, which asserts exporter output rows verbatim |
| Independent corroboration | `bitwarden/clients` `libs/importer/src/importers/spec-data/firefox-csv/{simple-password-data,firefox-accounts-data}.csv.ts` |
| Firefox version checked against | 149.0.2 |
| Generated on | 2026-07-29 |
| Generator | `./build-fixture.py`, committed next to the fixture so the bytes are reproducible (`python3 build-fixture.py` from the repo root) |

The export path this file stands in for is
about:logins → ⋯ → **Export Logins…**, which writes `logins.csv`.

## Exact header

```
"url","username","password","httpRealm","formActionOrigin","guid","timeCreated","timeLastUsed","timePasswordChanged"
```

Nine columns, every header cell quoted. `url` is the only renamed column — the
login property behind it is `origin`.

## Format rules this file pins

Straight from `_buildCSVRow` / `exportAsCSV`:

1. **Records are CRLF-separated and the file has no trailing newline.**
   `rows.map(e => e.join(",")).join("\r\n")` — the join produces no terminator
   after the final row.
2. **A `null`/`undefined` property writes a bare, unquoted empty field; an
   empty string writes `""`.** Both parse to `""`, so the distinction is
   invisible after parsing, but the raw bytes differ and a parser that assumes
   every field is quoted will break on the first form login.
3. **`"` inside a value is doubled** (`columnValue.split('"').join('""')`).
   No other character is escaped, and values are never trimmed.
4. **`httpRealm` and `formActionOrigin` are mutually exclusive.** A form login
   has `httpRealm` null; an HTTP-auth login has `formActionOrigin` null. Rows
   in this fixture cover both.
5. **Timestamps are epoch milliseconds written as strings**, and may be absent
   entirely (all three null) for a login that was never used.

## Coverage

| Case | Row |
| --- | --- |
| Plain form login | `https://github.com` |
| Non-ASCII username and password (`ö`, `ü`, `ß`) | `https://konto.example.de` |
| Empty-string username (`""`, not a null field) | `https://www.example.org` |
| Password containing a doubled quote and a comma | `https://quote.example.com` |
| HTTP-auth login: `httpRealm` set, `formActionOrigin` null | `https://intranet.example.com` |
| Firefox Sync account entry (skipped on import) | `chrome://FirefoxAccounts` |
| Port-qualified origin | `https://www7.example.com:8080` |
| `formActionOrigin` on a different host than the origin | `https://portal.example.com` |
| Empty-string `httpRealm` (must not become a field) | `http://legacy.example.net` |
| No guid and no timestamps at all | `file://` |

## Expected losses

Firefox's own lossiness — the export simply does not contain these:

- No item titles. Bittery derives a title from the URL host.
- No TOTP secrets, no notes, no folders, no custom fields, no attachments.
- Only saved website logins; nothing else Firefox stores.

Bittery's mapping decisions on top of that:

| Column | Outcome |
| --- | --- |
| `url` | `url` + `urls[0]`, and the source of the derived title |
| `username`, `password` | mapped directly |
| `httpRealm` | custom text field `HTTP Realm` when non-empty |
| `formActionOrigin` | **dropped.** It is autofill form-target metadata, not a page the user visits, and it regularly points at a different host (see the `https://portal.example.com` row). Importing it as a second URL would attach a login to a site it does not belong to. |
| `guid` | **dropped.** Source item ids are derived from the row number so they stay stable and unique regardless of what the exporter wrote. |
| `timeCreated`, `timeLastUsed`, `timePasswordChanged` | **dropped.** `DecryptedItemData` has no fields for them; Bittery stamps its own timestamps at import. |

The `chrome://FirefoxAccounts` row is skipped entirely with a
`sync-account-skipped` warning. It appears in every export taken from a
Sync-signed-in profile, and its "password" is a JSON blob of sync keys rather
than a credential. Bitwarden's importer filters the same row.

## Known gaps

- [ ] **A capture from a live Firefox run.** The obvious upgrade: seed a
      throwaway profile through about:logins → *Import from a File…*, export,
      and replace this file with what Firefox actually wrote. That would also
      supply real GUIDs and real timestamps.
- [ ] **A real Sync-account row.** The `chrome://FirefoxAccounts` row here has
      the right shape and quoting but fabricated key material; producing a
      genuine one requires signing into a Mozilla account.
- [ ] **A newline inside a quoted value.** Firefox's login manager rejects
      newlines in usernames and passwords, so no export can contain one. The
      parser handles it and the case is covered synthetically in
      `../../import-firefox.test.ts`.
- [ ] **`chrome://` extension logins** (`chrome://example_extension` in
      Mozilla's own test data) are not represented here.

Re-check `LoginExport.sys.mjs` on meaningful Firefox releases before widening
the accepted header.
